Problem: For some positive integers $n$, the numbers $2^n$ and $5^n$ have the same leading digit in their decimal representation. Find all such leading digits.

<reflection>
For the positive integers $n$ in question, $2^n$ and $5^n$ have the same leading digit $d$. The condition is that the first digit of $2^n$ equals the first digit of $5^n$, both equal to $d$. The numbers can be expressed in scientific notation with integer exponents $m$ and $p$.
In scientific notation the coefficients $a,b$ are real numbers in $[1,10)$, not necessarily integers. The leading digit is only the integer part of the coefficient, so this restriction is false and leads to the later invalid conclusion $a=b$.
Use logarithms to write $2^n=10^{n\log_{10}2}$ and $5^n=10^{n\log_{10}5}$, and compare the fractional parts of $n\log_{10}2$ and $n\log_{10}5$, using $2^n5^n=10^n$.
</reflection>
